_comment: Audio prompt pool v2 — ALL AFRO HOUSE. v1 diversified too far (nu-disco, 108 BPM downtempo, jazz ensemble, amapiano) and tracks stopped sounding like the channel's genre. Every variant now locks the Afro House DNA — four-on-the-floor house kick, 118-125 BPM, organic African percussion (congas, djembe, shakers), deep rolling bassline — and varies only the flavor on top (melodic, dark, tribal, organic, vocal, minimal...). Non-repetition window still applies.

prompts.prompt: Progressive Afro House, 122 BPM, four-on-the-floor. Heavy car-bass low end, organic percussion (congas, shakers, djembe, bongos), psychedelic tribal energy. Evolving atmospheric pads, subtle wordless tribal chants in wide stereo, dark synth arps rising to a cinematic festival drop. Spiritual yet raw, mastered for sub-bass impact. Mood: ritualistic, primal, transcendent.

Melodic Afro House for a sunrise set, 121 BPM, steady four-on-the-floor house kick with warm organic percussion. A tender piano motif and soft wordless vocal hum float over a deep rounded bassline; strings swell slowly like light breaking over the horizon. Unmistakably Afro House groove underneath the emotion. Mood: euphoric, luminous, hopeful.

Dark tribal Afro House, 120 BPM, relentless four-on-the-floor. Heavy ceremonial toms and djembe locked to a deep rolling bassline, ominous drone pads, distant ritual chant fragments. Metallic percussion accents like ritual bells, tension building in long hypnotic waves. Mood: ominous, hypnotic, powerful.

Organic Afro House, 120 BPM, warm four-on-the-floor groove. Field-recording textures (birdsong, water, wooden clicks) woven around hand-played congas and shakers, earthy deep bassline, soft mallet chords and acoustic guitar plucks riding the house pulse. Sun-warmed and alive, but always a dancefloor groove. Mood: natural, soulful, uplifting.

Peak-time Afro House / Afro Tech, 124 BPM, driving four-on-the-floor for a festival main stage. Punchy layered tribal drums, tight aggressive bassline, filtered build-ups with white-noise risers and a euphoric hands-in-the-air drop with a chopped vocal stab. Loud, wide, relentless. Mood: explosive, ecstatic.

Minimal hypnotic Afro House, 120 BPM, stripped four-on-the-floor. One rolling marimba loop, dry kick, tight shaker, a single deep sub note that breathes. Long patient grooves where the tension lives between the hits — late-night warehouse Afro House, nothing extra. Mood: hypnotic, restrained, meditative.

Vocal Afro House, 122 BPM, four-on-the-floor with rich organic drums. Call-and-response African chants (wordless, soulful) over a deep melodic bassline, warm piano stabs and handclaps; a goosebump choir swell in the breakdown, then back into the rolling groove. Mood: communal, uplifting, spiritual.

Afro House with a desert flavor, 119 BPM, solid four-on-the-floor foundation. Snaking oud-like plucked strings and a distant female ululation ride over frame drums, shakers and a dry deep sub bassline. Mysterious and cinematic, but the house groove never stops driving. Mood: mysterious, ancient, hypnotic.

Deep rolling Afro House for 3 a.m., 123 BPM, tunnel-vision four-on-the-floor. A relentless rolling bassline drives everything; tight dry drums, hissing hats, one slowly mutating synth blip, sparse tribal percussion accents. Almost no melody — pure forward momentum. Mood: dark, driving, hypnotic.

Cinematic Afro House, 120 BPM, four-on-the-floor with tribal drums at the core. Orchestral string swells and a lone horn theme rise over the groove; timpani rolls punctuate the builds, quiet intimate breakdowns opening into vast emotional peaks — but the Afro House pulse never drops out. Mood: epic, sweeping, powerful.

Warm groovy Afro House, 121 BPM, bouncy four-on-the-floor. Rounded melodic bassline, crisp organic percussion, jazzy electric-piano chords and a tasteful sax lick floating over the groove; finger snaps and soft vocal chops keep it playful. Feel-good sunset Afro House. Mood: smooth, joyful, warm.

Drum-heavy tribal Afro House, 123 BPM, pounding four-on-the-floor. Layered djembe, talking drum and shaker in call-and-response over a deep anchoring sub; gang vocal chants answering the drums, raw skin-and-wood texture with field-recording grit — all locked to the house pulse. Mood: primal, communal, energetic.
